newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late gains with firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late gains with firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held modest gains late Thursday in fairly active trade, with stronger physical prices still boosting the complex despite mostly bearish weather forecasts, market sources said.
At 1425 EDT, September was still up by 3.3 cents at $2.505 per million British thermal units, while October was 3.7 cents higher at $2.53. Most others were steady to up 4.2 cents.
"Supply and demand must be tighter than people think, but there's still not a lot of support from the weather," said one Midwest trader, referring to another cooling trend next week.
After a brief weekend warmup in the Midwest and Northeast, temperatures next week in most regions are expected to drift around normal though hot weather should stay in the West.
While Wednesday's weekly stock build of 78 bcf was in line with expectations, traders said concerns about lagging stocks to 1994 and 1995 levels were still lending support.
In addition, fund buying, apparent again yesterday with another jump in open interest to record levels, also helped fuel the recent rally.
"The funds still like the market and they're big-time long, but if we don't break to new intraday highs today (above $2.55 in September), you could see some people bail," an East Coast trader said.
Hub open interest on August 13 climbed 7,561 contracts to a record 223,148, with the bulk of the gain coming in October, while September was down slightly.

Technical traders pegged key September resistance at the contract high and double top at $2.605, with further selling likely at the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January. Support was seen at $2.405, $2.34 and $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27.

In the cash Thursday, Gulf Coast prices jumped more than a a dime to the low-to-mid $2.50s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the low-to-mid $2.40s. New York city gate gas gained 10-15 cents to the low-to-mid $2.70s.
NYMEX said 35,995 contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
On the KCBT, September climbed 1.5 cents to $2.41, while deferreds were steady to 3.5 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 1.8 cents to 9.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
